messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test asserts that the XPath expression “//location[2]/following::node()[2]” should resolve to the pointer “/vendor[1]/product[1]”. In XPath, node() matches any node type (elements, text, comments, processing instructions, etc.) on the selected axis. The “following” axis includes all nodes in document order after the context node (excluding attribute and namespace nodes, which aren’t on the “following” axis).

How the code processes this:
- The following axis is implemented via PrecedingOrFollowingContext.nextNode. It walks nodes in document order after the current context node and, for each visited node, calls currentNodePointer.testNode(nodeTest) to decide if it matches the user-specified node test.
- For node(), nodeTest is a NodeTypeTest with type NODE. The dispatch lands in DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node, NodeTest).

The bug:
- In DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node, NodeTest), for NodeTypeTest with NODE, the code returns true only for ELEMENT_NODE or DOCUMENT_NODE:
  - case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE: return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
- This is incorrect per XPath semantics. node() should match any node type. Because of this, text nodes (e.g., whitespace between elements) and other non-element nodes are excluded from matches along the following axis.

Why the test fails:
- The document under test apparently has a text node immediately following the second location node. With correct node() semantics, that text node would be the first following::node(), making the second following::node() the element /vendor[1]/product[1], as the test expects.
- Due to the bug, text nodes are ignored, so the first counted node is the first following element. Consequently, the second counted node is not /vendor[1]/product[1], and the assertion fails.

This matches the current issue report, which points out that node() is erroneously restricted to elements and the document node in DOMNodePointer (and similarly in the JDOM implementation). The fix is to make the case for NODE_TYPE_NODE accept any node type (i.e., return true).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
